phenological_overlap.workbook_shape: 45 plants x 135 pollinators plus row/column labels
phenological_overlap.source_definition: number of weeks across the entire six-year sampling period in which each plant-pollinator pair co-occurred

flower_abundance.source_definition: flower counts summed across years to obtain one overall abundance per plant species over the entire six-year sampling period

consequence_for_cross_validation.held_out_object: annual link outcome rows for one transition
consequence_for_cross_validation.not_held_out: the temporal support used to construct study-wide phenological overlap and overall flower abundance
forbidden_labels: temporal extrapolation with all predictors estimated only from training years

interpretation: The annual CV still asks whether study-wide independently tabulated ecological filters discriminate link gains and losses in a held-out annual transition. It does not establish that those filters would forecast a future transition when estimated using only information available beforehand.

impact_on_existing_result.phenology_block_result: retained as a held-out response predictive-filter result
impact_on_existing_result.gain_loss_asymmetry: retained as a retrospective held-out discrimination asymmetry

claim_ceiling: Use the annual Villavicencio analysis as a retrospective external-response bridge and feasibility result. Do not describe it as a prospective forecast until year-specific or genuinely past-only covariates are reconstructed.
